summary: A sound IELTS-format listening test: four parts of the right type and length, and every part has real traps (corrections, options mentioned and then rejected). Parts 1 and 4 are a little easier than the real test because the form and notes repeat the speakers' words almost exactly, so the paper is a fair 6.5-7 practice rather than a hard one.
strengths: Part 1 has proper IELTS traps: a misheard date corrected (12th/21st), a price corrected (100 to 80 thousand), a time withdrawn (11.15 to 10.30), a day withdrawn (Monday), and telephone rejected for email.
Part 2 and Part 3 MCQs each mention and reject the two wrong options before the right one, as in the real test.
Part 3 multi-select items test listening for what is NOT borrowed or NOT needed (tripod, tape, sample bags; tide table, coastguard, printing), which is genuine IELTS style.
Part 4 is a coherent academic lecture of about 775 words; the notes follow the order of the talk and every answer is one word, spelled as heard.
Answers appear in question order in every part.

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair broken: 'replaced with' does not occur in the script (the lecturer says 'replaced animal fat with olive oil').
issues.change: Pair now ['replaced animal fat with olive oil', 'used olive oil in place of animal'].

issues.problem: Box option A 'will run more often' repeats the lecturer's exact words 'it will simply run more often', so the item needs no paraphrase recognition.
issues.change: Suggest rewording option A to 'will have a more frequent service'.

issues.problem: Box option F 'will be extended to a new terminus' copies 'extended' and 'terminus' from the script.
issues.change: Suggest 'will go further than it does now' so students must link it to 'extended past the retail park'.

issues.problem: Part 1 (572 words) is at the short end, and most form rows (address, occupation, appointment, medication, reminder) repeat the speakers' wording, so Questions 1-4 and 6-9 carry no paraphrase.
issues.change: Acceptable for Part 1. For a harder version, reword some rows (e.g. 'Job' instead of 'Occupation', 'Medicines to list' instead of 'a list of any ... she takes regularly').

issues.problem: Several Part 4 note lines are near-copies of the lecture sentences (31, 32, 37, 38, 39), which makes Part 4 a little easier than a real Part 4.
issues.change: In future sets, paraphrase more of the note stems (e.g. 'soap was one of the earliest branded goods' for 38).
